title: Types of Weather
keyIdea: Weather types name what the sky and air are doing today: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy or snowy. Watch for clues like bright sun, falling drops, thick cloud, pushing air or cold white flakes.
familyTip: Each morning for a week, look out of the window together and pick one weather word. Snap a quick photo and sort the week into sunny / rainy / cloudy / windy / snowy piles.

visual.caption: Weather words — fair idea or myth? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: sunny means bright sun and clear sky
weather is the same word as season
rainy means drops falling from clouds
windy always means it must be winter
cloudy means thick cloud covering the sky

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name sunny, rainy, cloudy and windy days; match a snowy card; then challenge.

kid: Sunny means a bright sun and a clear sky.
Rainy means drops falling from clouds.
Cloudy means thick cloud. Windy means the air pushes hard.
Snowy means cold white flakes. Weather is about today — not a whole season.
adult: KS1 science / geography: observe and describe weather types (sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, snowy). Keep weather (today’s sky and air) separate from season (a longer stretch) and from clothing choices.
Common mistakes: using weather and season as the same word; thinking windy only happens in winter; naming clothes instead of sky clues; missing that cloudy can hide the sun without rain.
In the lab your child names four sky types, matches a snowy day card, rejects season/coat myths, then tries challenge traps for those slips.

practice.prompt: You spot {n} different weather types this week. How many types did you spot?
practice.hint: The count of types you named is the answer.
practice.explain: You named {n} weather types across the week.

practice.prompt: A chart shows {n} days. {k} were rainy. How many days were not rainy?
practice.hint: Subtract the rainy days from the total.
practice.explain: {n} days minus {k} rainy leaves {=n-k} that were not rainy.

practice.prompt: Order from brightest sun clue to coldest flake clue.
practice.hint: Start with the clear bright sky, end with snow.
practice.explain: Sunny first, then cloudy, then snowy.
